title: Coin Change II
statement: Given coin denominations `coins` (unlimited supply of each) and an `amount`, return the number of **combinations** of coins that add up to `amount`. Order does not matter: `1 + 2` and `2 + 1` are the same combination.
idea: Let `dp[a]` be the number of ways to make amount `a` using the coin types allowed so far. With no coins, only amount 0 can be made — in exactly one way.
Introduce the coins **one type at a time**. With a new coin `c`, every way to make `a − c` gives one more way to make `a` (append one `c`): `dp[a] += dp[a − c]`.
Because a coin type is finished before the next one starts, each combination is built in one fixed order of coin types — so `1 + 2` and `2 + 1` are not counted twice.

complexity.timeWhy: Every amount is updated once per coin type.

steps.text: Our example: **`amount = 5, coins = [1,2,5]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
There is exactly **1** way to make amount 0: take no coins. Every other amount has 0 ways so far.
